sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions About SEO Services

items.title: What are SEO services?
paragraphs: SEO services improve how a website is discovered and understood by search engines. They may include technical SEO, keyword research, on-page optimisation, content planning, local SEO, internal linking and performance tracking.

items.title: How long does SEO take to show results?
paragraphs: SEO timelines depend on the website’s current condition, competition, market, content quality and technical setup. Some improvements may appear earlier, while stronger and more consistent growth usually requires ongoing work over several months.

items.title: Can you guarantee first-page rankings?
paragraphs: No responsible SEO professional can guarantee a specific ranking position. Search results depend on competition, search algorithms, website quality and many external factors. The focus should be on consistent improvements in relevance, visibility, traffic and conversions.

items.title: Do I need ongoing SEO?
paragraphs: Ongoing SEO is recommended for businesses operating in competitive or changing markets. Search behaviour, competitors, content and website performance change over time, so continued optimisation helps maintain and improve visibility.

items.title: Can you work on my existing website?
paragraphs: Yes. I can review and optimise an existing website when the platform and technical setup allow the required changes. The first step is usually an SEO audit to identify the most important issues.

items.title: Do you provide local SEO?
paragraphs: Yes. Local SEO support can include Google Business Profile optimisation, local keyword research, location-page optimisation, citation review and Google Maps visibility recommendations.

items.title: Do you provide ecommerce SEO?
paragraphs: Yes. Ecommerce SEO can include category-page optimisation, product-page recommendations, technical reviews, internal linking, content planning and structured data recommendations.

items.title: Is content necessary for SEO?
paragraphs: Content is important because it helps search engines and potential customers understand your services, products and expertise. The exact content required depends on the website and search opportunities.

items.title: Can SEO and Google Ads be used together?
paragraphs: Yes. SEO and Google Ads can support the same search strategy. Ads can provide more immediate visibility, while SEO builds a stronger long-term organic presence.

items.title: How do you measure SEO performance?
paragraphs: Performance can be measured through search visibility, impressions, clicks, organic traffic, keyword movement, landing-page engagement and enquiries or sales generated through organic search.

items.title: How much do SEO services cost?
paragraphs: SEO pricing depends on the website size, market competition, current issues, number of pages, locations and level of ongoing support. A customised proposal is provided after reviewing your requirements.

sections.title: Are Your Google Ads Producing Clicks but Not Enough Business?
paragraphs: A campaign can generate traffic without delivering enough qualified enquiries or sales. Poor search targeting, weak conversion tracking, unclear advertisements and disconnected landing pages can all reduce the value of your advertising budget.

sections.title: Understanding the Different Types of Google Ads Campaigns
paragraphs: Google Ads provides several campaign types for reaching users across Search, YouTube, websites, applications, shopping results and Google-owned feeds. The right choice depends on whether your objective is to capture existing demand, generate new interest, promote products, increase app usage or reconnect with previous visitors.

items.title: Search Campaigns
paragraphs: Search campaigns display text-based advertisements around relevant Google searches. They are primarily used to reach people who are already looking for a product, service, provider or solution connected to your business.
Search campaigns offer direct control over areas such as keywords, search terms, advertisement messaging, locations and negative keywords.
Google describes Search campaigns as a way to show advertisements around relevant searches across its Search Network.

items.title: Performance Max Campaigns
paragraphs: Performance Max is a goal-based campaign type that can access Google advertising inventory across channels such as Search, YouTube, Display, Discover, Gmail and Maps from one campaign.

Rather than controlling each placement independently, advertisers provide conversion goals, audience signals, creative assets, budgets and business information. Google then uses automation to identify opportunities across its inventory.
Performance Max is designed to complement keyword-based Search campaigns while accessing inventory across Google’s channels.

groups.label: Best suited for
items: Lead generation across multiple Google channels
Advertisers with strong image and video assets

items.title: Demand Gen Campaigns
paragraphs: Demand Gen campaigns use visually engaging image, video and product advertisements to reach users while they browse Google’s feed-based and visual environments.

They can serve across placements including YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Discover, Gmail, Maps and the Google Display Network. These campaigns are useful when potential customers may not yet be actively searching but could respond to a relevant message or offer.
Demand Gen campaigns are designed to drive engagement and action across Google’s major visual and feed-based surfaces.

groups.label: Best suited for
items: Moving users from awareness towards conversion

items.title: Shopping Campaigns
paragraphs: Shopping campaigns promote ecommerce products using information submitted through Google Merchant Center.

Rather than relying mainly on standard text advertisements, Shopping ads can display product details such as the image, title, price and store name. This helps users understand the offer before visiting the website.
Shopping campaigns require accurate product information, clear conversion measurement and a website that supports a reliable purchasing experience.

items.title: Video Campaigns
paragraphs: Video campaigns allow businesses to advertise through video content on YouTube and participating Google video partners.
Depending on the selected objective and format, video can support reach, awareness, product consideration, website visits and selected conversion goals.
Google notes that Video campaigns can display advertisements across YouTube and websites or applications using Google video partners.

groups.label: Best suited for
items: Building familiarity before a search or purchase

items.title: Display Campaigns
paragraphs: Display campaigns use visual advertisements across websites, applications and Google Display Network placements.
They can support broad reach, visual promotion and remarketing. Display campaigns generally target audiences, placements, topics or user behaviour rather than relying only on active search terms.
Display should be planned carefully because broad targeting can generate visibility without necessarily producing qualified business outcomes.

items.title: App Campaigns
paragraphs: App campaigns are designed to promote mobile applications across Google properties such as Search, Google Play, YouTube, Discover and the Display Network.
Advertisers provide basic text, images, videos and campaign goals. Google then automatically creates and serves different advertisement combinations.
Google states that App campaigns can promote applications across several of its largest properties, including Search, Play, YouTube, Discover and the Display Network.

items.title: Which Campaign Type Should You Choose?
paragraphs: The right campaign type depends on the customer journey and the result you want to generate.
A business may use more than one campaign type, but each campaign should have a clear purpose. Adding more campaign types does not automatically improve performance.

groups.label: Business objective / Recommended campaign type
items: Generate leads across Google channels — Performance Max
Promote ecommerce products — Shopping or Performance Max
Reach visually engaged audiences — Demand Gen
Reconnect with website visitors — Demand Gen or Display
